question: A hollow conducting shell is kept in electrostatic equilibrium and no charge is placed inside its hollow region. Explain why the electric field inside the hollow region is zero. Also justify why the potential is constant throughout the conductor and the hollow region.

options.A: In electrostatic equilibrium, fields inside the conducting material are zero. With no charge in the cavity, induced surface charges shield it so the cavity field is zero; therefore no potential difference exists and potential is constant throughout the conductor and cavity
options.B: The cavity field is non-zero because every hollow region contains electric field; potential changes linearly through the conductor
options.C: The cavity field is zero only if the conductor is uncharged; potential is always zero everywhere
options.D: The cavity field is uniform and the potential is constant only on the outer surface
